title: Is Ukraine Turning the Tide in the War?

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是Benjamin Poulin，我是Mark Ronson，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店打碟的黑胶唱片时代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，陈列着那些精美的、有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的Sabrina Tavernisi，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: The tide appears to be turning in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰战局似乎正在发生转变。

sentences.en: Ukrainian forces claiming to have retaken more than 40 towns in just a matter of days.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰军队声称在短短几天内收复了40多个城镇。

sentences.en: Crippling Russia's grip in the Kharkiv region and forcing the Russians to retreat.
sentences.zh: 削弱了俄罗斯在哈尔科夫地区的控制力，并迫使俄军撤退。

sentences.en: Over the weekend, the Ukrainian military stunned the world by taking hundreds of miles of territory back from Russia.
sentences.zh: 周末期间，乌克兰军队从俄罗斯手中夺回了数百英里的领土，震惊了世界。

sentences.en: Ukrainian troops have raised their flag in multiple towns and villages previously occupied by Russian troops.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰军队已经在多个此前被俄军占领的城镇和村庄升起了国旗。

sentences.en: Their biggest victory since the beginning of the war.
sentences.zh: 这是自战争开始以来他们取得的最大胜利。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Eric Schmidt on Ukraine's success, Russia's failure, and how the war in Ukraine has reached a critical point.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事Eric Schmidt将探讨乌克兰的成功、俄罗斯的失败，以及乌克兰战争如何进入了一个关键节点。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, September 13th.
sentences.zh: 今天是9月13日，星期二。

sentences.en: So, Eric, we've been seeing all of these headlines coming out of Ukraine over the weekend about how there have been this string of successes,
sentences.zh: Eric，周末我们看到所有关于乌克兰的新闻头条都在说那里取得了一连串的成功，

sentences.en: how the Ukrainian military has made this huge advance.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰军队取得了巨大的进展。

sentences.en: And that seems kind of remarkable, right?
sentences.zh: 这看起来相当了不起，对吧？

sentences.en: Because in a lot of ways, the war had really settled into this kind of stalemate for a number of months now.
sentences.zh: 因为在很多方面，这场战争已经陷入僵局好几个月了。

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我想确实如此。

sentences.en: It really was kind of a grinding conflict.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一场磨人的冲突。

sentences.en: And what we saw was over the weekend and a few days before that was a sharp jolt that kind of jump-started the war again with this dramatic blitzkrieg on the part of the Ukrainians.
sentences.zh: 而我们在周末以及之前几天看到的是一次剧烈的震荡，通过乌克兰人发动的这场戏剧性的闪电战，让战争重新焕发了活力。

sentences.en: So, how did the Ukrainians pull it off?
sentences.zh: 那么，乌克兰人是怎么做到的呢？

sentences.en: Well, I think to understand that, you need to go back several months, you know,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为要理解这一点，你需要回顾几个月前，你知道，

sentences.en: to the spring and April timeframe when the Russians experienced their first real major setback of the war, where they sought to topple the government in Kiev in a matter of days.
sentences.zh: 回到春季和四月份的时候，当时俄罗斯经历了战争中第一次真正的重大挫折，他们曾试图在几天内推翻基辅政府。

sentences.en: And it was a dramatic failure.
sentences.zh: 结果是一场惨败。

sentences.en: If you remember, we saw that long convoy of Russian trucks coming in from the north and just being picked off.
sentences.zh: 如果你还记得，我们当时看到那支从北方开来的长长的俄罗斯卡车车队，简直就是活靶子。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They're stuck.
sentences.zh: 他们被困住了。

sentences.en: And the Russians totally underestimated the Ukrainians.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人完全低估了乌克兰人。

sentences.en: They took heavy casualties.
sentences.zh: 他们伤亡惨重。

sentences.en: And they ultimately had to retreat in humiliating fashion with their tail between their legs.
sentences.zh: 最终不得不以一种屈辱的方式夹着尾巴撤退。

sentences.en: And as they leave, the dust settles.
sentences.zh: 当他们离开后，尘埃落定。

sentences.en: And these first few first months of the war, you see kind of three fronts emerging in this war.
sentences.zh: 在战争的最初几个月里，你可以看到这场战争中出现了三个战线。

sentences.en: And Eric, remind us what those three fronts are.
sentences.zh: Eric，提醒我们一下那三个战线是什么。

sentences.en: So, the immediate next front is the one in the Donbass, where the Russians had regrouped.
sentences.zh: 紧接着的下一个战线是顿巴斯地区，俄罗斯人在那里进行了重组。

sentences.en: They focus on their strength in the east, closer to their supply lines.
sentences.zh: 他们专注于自己在东部的优势，那里离他们的补给线更近。

sentences.en: And they use one of their main weapons of choice, artillery.
sentences.zh: 他们使用了他们最主要的武器之一：火炮。

sentences.en: And they've got a lot of it to just shell the Ukrainian positions and start taking back more areas of the eaSt.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有大量的火炮，用来轰炸乌克兰阵地，并开始夺回东部更多的地区。

sentences.en: The second front is the area in around the city of Kharkiv in the northeast, where the Ukrainians are basically holding on.
sentences.zh: 第二条战线是东北部哈尔科夫市周边地区，乌克兰人基本上是在那里坚守。

sentences.en: They've kept the Russians out of the city.
sentences.zh: 他们把俄罗斯人挡在了城市之外。

sentences.en: But there's basically a standstill in keeping the Russians from advancing any further.
sentences.zh: 但基本上处于僵持状态，阻止了俄罗斯人进一步推进。

sentences.en: And the final and perhaps most important front is the one in the south, called Kherson.
sentences.zh: 最后，也许是最重要的战线是南部的赫尔松。

sentences.en: And this is really kind of the real prize for both sides because of its access to the Black Sea, its access to water and power resources.
sentences.zh: 由于它通往黑海，拥有水资源和电力资源，这确实是双方真正的必争之地。

sentences.en: So, that really is a focal point for all sides as this war kind of shapes up.
sentences.zh: 所以，随着战争形势的发展，这确实是各方的焦点。

sentences.en: But by midsummer, we're looking at basically, you know, front lines not really changing much on any one of these three.
sentences.zh: 但到了仲夏，基本上，你知道，这三条战线上的前线并没有发生太大变化。

sentences.en: And it's looking like it's going to be a very long war of attrition.
sentences.zh: 看起来这将是一场非常漫长的消耗战。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It looked like, you know, you looked at the map and you saw the three fronts and it wasn't changing very much.
sentences.zh: 看起来，你知道，你看着地图，看到了三条战线，但并没有什么太大的变化。

sentences.en: I mean, it was just sort of the to and fro, a bit of territory here, a bit of territory there.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这只是一种来回拉锯，这里占领一点领土，那里占领一点领土。

sentences.en: But no one was really winning in one direction or the other.
sentences.zh: 但没有人真正向任何一个方向取得决定性胜利。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And, you know, what's happened here is we come out of the summer is there are some important changes are about to happen.
sentences.zh: 你知道，随着夏天过去，这里发生了一些即将到来的重要变化。

sentences.en: The first major change is that all these Western weapons, billions of dollars of armaments, mostly from the United States, but also from a wide range, dozens of other countries,
sentences.zh: 第一个重大变化是，所有这些西方武器，价值数十亿美元的军火，大部分来自美国，但也来自其他几十个国家，

sentences.en: starts pouring into Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 开始源源不断地涌入乌克兰。

sentences.en: And the Ukrainian military is able to use these weapons much more effectively.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰军队能够更有效地使用这些武器。

sentences.en: And what are those weapons, Eric?
sentences.zh: Eric，那些是什么武器？

sentences.en: Tell me a little bit about them.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲它们。

sentences.en: So some of these weapons, we've talked about them on the show before.
sentences.zh: 其中一些武器，我们之前在节目中讨论过。

sentences.en: The one that many people remember is the HIMARS.
sentences.zh: 很多人记得的一种是“海马斯”（HIMARS）。

sentences.en: And this is basically a missile launching system that can fire satellite guided missiles that carry 200 pounds of explosives almost 50 miles away at targets.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是一种导弹发射系统，可以发射卫星制导导弹，携带200磅炸药，打击近50英里外的目标。

sentences.en: And these are critical because these weapons in the hands of the Ukrainians can now hit Russian supply depots.
sentences.zh: 这些武器至关重要，因为在乌克兰人手中，它们现在可以打击俄罗斯的补给站。

sentences.en: They can hit command posts.
sentences.zh: 它们可以打击指挥所。

sentences.en: They can hit radars well behind the front lines.
sentences.zh: 它们可以打击前线后方的雷达。

sentences.en: And this causes havoc with the Russians and with their ability to supply, you know, maintain their supply routes to these different places.
sentences.zh: 这给俄罗斯人造成了严重破坏，影响了他们向不同地点维持补给路线的能力。

sentences.en: So Ukrainians are suddenly hitting much farther and much deeper into enemy territory than they have ever had before.
sentences.zh: 所以乌克兰人突然能够比以往任何时候都更远、更深入地打击敌方领土。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But these weapons deliveries carry another major advantage for the Ukrainians.
sentences.zh: 但这些武器的交付为乌克兰人带来了另一个重大优势。

sentences.en: And that is, at this point, the Pentagon is announcing every week or so another 500 million to a billion dollars worth of additional weapons and ammunition.
sentences.zh: 那就是，此时此刻，五角大楼几乎每周都会宣布额外提供5亿到10亿美元的武器和弹药。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And what this does, this kind of regularity, it allows Ukrainian commanders who are now having to start thinking about
sentences.zh: 这种规律性所带来的影响是，它让乌克兰指挥官们能够开始考虑，

sentences.en: planning much more complex operations, simultaneous offensive along these different fronts.
sentences.zh: 规划更复杂的行动，在这些不同战线上同时发动进攻。

sentences.en: They need to know in advance that they're going to have enough weapons and arms to carry this out.
sentences.zh: 他们需要提前知道他们将有足够的武器和装备来执行这些计划。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They have to plan.
sentences.zh: 他们必须进行规划。

sentences.en: Yeah, they've got to plan.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们必须规划。

sentences.en: And this gives them the confidence to start planning what we now see as kind of unfolding, these very complicated operations that take a lot of ammunition to carry out.
sentences.zh: 这给了他们信心，开始规划我们现在看到的正在展开的这些非常复杂的行动，这些行动需要大量的弹药才能完成。

sentences.en: You know, they're fast-moving operations, and you need a lot of equipment and material on hand to be able to do this and have confidence it's going to laSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是快速移动的行动，你需要手头有大量的装备和物资，才能做到这一点，并确信它能持续下去。

sentences.en: So what's the other thing that changed over the summer, Eric?
sentences.zh: 那么夏天发生的另一件事是什么，Eric？

sentences.en: So the other big development late in the summer is that the intelligence sharing between the Ukrainians and the Americans just got a lot better.
sentences.zh: 夏天晚些时候的另一个重大进展是，乌克兰和美国之间的情报共享变得好多了。

sentences.en: And we can see this now in the way this whole campaign is unfolding.
sentences.zh: 我们现在可以从整个战役的展开方式中看出这一点。

sentences.en: Because what the Ukrainians did was they started sharing a lot more details about their operational planning, basically their campaign plans for these various fronts.
sentences.zh: 因为乌克兰人所做的是，他们开始分享更多关于他们作战计划的细节，基本上是他们针对这些不同战线的战役计划。

sentences.en: And in doing so, by showing what they intended to do, the Americans then could go back and look at their intelligence and give more specific advice to the Ukrainians and say,
sentences.zh: 通过展示他们的意图，美国人随后可以回过头来查看他们的情报，并向乌克兰人提供更具体的建议，说，

sentences.en: where are some more targeted vulnerabilities along these Russian lines?
sentences.zh: 在这些俄罗斯防线上，哪里还有更具针对性的弱点？

sentences.en: Where are these offensives that you have planned?
sentences.zh: 你们计划的这些进攻在哪里？

sentences.en: Where they'd be more effective?
sentences.zh: 在哪里会更有效？

sentences.en: And so you had a much broader sense of cooperation and sharing between what the Ukrainians were planning
sentences.zh: 因此，在乌克兰人计划的内容与美国人如何帮助促进和改进这些计划之间，你们有了更广泛的合作和共享。

sentences.en: in terms of their ground campaign and how the Americans could help facilitate and improve on that.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是美国人提供情报，乌克兰人拿去随心所欲地使用。

sentences.en: It wasn't just the Americans providing intelligence and the Ukrainians taking that and doing what they will.
sentences.zh: 在这场战争的关键阶段，情报共享程度大大提高了。

sentences.en: It was a much greater intelligence sharing at this crucial phase of the war.
sentences.zh: 这是战争关键阶段情报共享的极大提升。

sentences.en: And in the meantime, Ukraine is under quite a bit of time pressure, right?
sentences.zh: 与此同时，乌克兰面临着相当大的时间压力，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, I remember we did an episode earlier in the summer about how the Europeans were really starting to feel pretty frustrated with Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我记得我们在夏天早些时候做过一期节目，关于欧洲人如何开始对乌克兰感到相当沮丧。

sentences.en: You know, wanting it to kind of get on track towards some sort of resolution because they had problems of their own.
sentences.zh: 你知道，希望它能朝着某种解决方案走上正轨，因为他们自己也有问题。

sentences.en: They didn't want to be spending so much time on Ukraine and its probleMs.
sentences.zh: 他们不想在乌克兰及其问题上花费太多时间。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Ukraine begins to feel kind of a self-imposed sense of urgency to make a major move.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰开始感到一种自我施加的紧迫感，需要采取重大行动。

sentences.en: I mean, politically, President Zelensky feels he needs to score a major victory
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从政治上讲，泽连斯基总统觉得他需要取得一场重大胜利，

sentences.en: to keep Western supporters on board going into the winter months when he knows that President Putin is going to put the screws to Europe in terms of energy,
sentences.zh: 以在进入冬季时留住西方支持者，因为他知道普京总统将在能源方面对欧洲施加压力，

sentences.en: cutting back on their energy sources.
sentences.zh: 削减他们的能源供应。

sentences.en: And he's fearing that if they don't demonstrate that they can score a big win, they're going to lose that critical support from Europeans.
sentences.zh: 他担心如果他们不能证明自己能取得大胜，他们就会失去欧洲人那份关键的支持。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: At the same time, though, the military commanders are concerned because they feel they need to make some gains on the ground before winter sets in
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，军事指挥官们很担心，因为他们觉得需要在冬天到来之前在地面上取得一些进展，

sentences.en: because militarily, it just becomes much harder to maneuver and the battle lines become literally frozen over there.
sentences.zh: 因为从军事上讲，机动变得困难得多，战线在那里实际上会冻结。

sentences.en: And so there's both this political urgency and, to some extent, you know, a military urgency to carry out some, you know, major offensives on the ground.
sentences.zh: 所以既有这种政治上的紧迫性，在某种程度上，也有在地面上进行一些重大进攻的军事紧迫性。

sentences.en: And so the clock is ticking.
sentences.zh: 所以时间在流逝。

sentences.en: So what does the Ukrainian military do?
sentences.zh: 那么乌克兰军队做了什么？

sentences.en: So President Zelensky favors a huge operation to push to the south to try and reclaim much of that territory there, perhaps going all the way to Mariupol and the Black Sea.
sentences.zh: 泽连斯基总统倾向于采取大规模行动向南推进，试图收复那里的大部分领土，也许一直打到马里乌波尔和黑海。

sentences.en: American advisers look at this plan, remember, they're sharing information more now, and say, boy, that's very risky and it's not likely to work.
sentences.zh: 美国顾问们审视了这个计划，记住，他们现在分享信息更多了，他们说，天哪，这太冒险了，不太可能成功。

sentences.en: But how about we try this?
sentences.zh: 但我们试试这个怎么样？

sentences.en: Let's break it into two parts.
sentences.zh: 让我们把它分成两部分。

sentences.en: Let's still have an offensive in the south, in Kherson.
sentences.zh: 让我们仍然在南部，在赫尔松进行进攻。

sentences.en: Remember, that's still the main prize.
sentences.zh: 记住，那仍然是主要目标。

sentences.en: But by telegraphing that offensive will draw Russian soldiers away from other parts.
sentences.zh: 但通过发出进攻信号，我们将把俄罗斯士兵从其他地方吸引过来。

sentences.en: We'll draw forces away from the north in Kharkiv, and they'll bring them down to the south.
sentences.zh: 我们将把兵力从北部的哈尔科夫吸引走，他们会把兵力调到南部。

sentences.en: And that will leave that northern part more vulnerable to a second attack.
sentences.zh: 这将使北部地区更容易受到第二次攻击。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So kind of like a fake-out.
sentences.zh: 所以有点像假动作。

sentences.en: A little bit.
sentences.zh: 有一点。

sentences.en: But remember, there is actually still fighting in Kherson.
sentences.zh: 但请记住，赫尔松实际上仍然有战斗。

sentences.en: It's not a total feint.
sentences.zh: 这不是完全的佯攻。

sentences.en: But what it's done is it's pulled away thousands of some of the best Russian troops north of this and left some serious gaps up along this flanking area outside of Kharkiv.
sentences.zh: 但它所做的是，它吸引走了数千名最优秀的俄罗斯军队，留下了哈尔科夫外围侧翼地区的一些严重缺口。

sentences.en: And this is where the Ukrainians strike and where we see this blitzkrieg on the ground just last week where they punch through several thousand well-armed Ukrainian forces
sentences.zh: 这就是乌克兰人发动打击的地方，也是我们上周在地面上看到的闪电战，他们突破了数千名装备精良的乌克兰部队，

sentences.en: and essentially rout the Russians that are remaining there to the point where Russian soldiers are just throwing down their arms,
sentences.zh: 基本上击溃了留在那里的俄罗斯人，以至于俄罗斯士兵只是扔掉武器，

sentences.en: they're jumping out of their tanks and other equipment, and they're fleeing on foot.
sentences.zh: 他们跳下坦克和其他装备，徒步逃跑。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And the Ukrainians themselves, I mean, they had hoped they might have some success up there.
sentences.zh: 而乌克兰人自己，我的意思是，他们曾希望在那里取得一些成功。

sentences.en: They're stunned by how successful they are as they push this offensive forward.
sentences.zh: 他们对推进这次进攻所取得的成功感到震惊。

sentences.en: And within a matter of days, the Ukrainians have seized what they say is more than a thousand square miles.
sentences.zh: 在短短几天内，乌克兰人已经夺取了他们所说的超过一千平方英里的土地。

sentences.en: That's roughly the size of Rhode Island.
sentences.zh: 这大约相当于罗德岛州的大小。

sentences.en: Remember, this is after months at both sides, just barely eking out a kilometer here, a kilometer there.
sentences.zh: 记住，这是在双方几个月来仅仅在这里推进一公里，那里推进一公里的情况下发生的。

sentences.en: And so this is really significant in terms of this bolt that the Ukrainian forces are making,
sentences.zh: 所以，就乌克兰军队发动的这次突袭而言，这确实意义重大，

sentences.en: pushing them east, back toward Russia, away from Kharkiv in this northeastern part of the country.
sentences.zh: 将他们向东推回俄罗斯，远离该国东北部的哈尔科夫。

sentences.en: So it sounds like the story of the weekend is really one of sudden and in a lot of ways surprising Ukrainian success.
sentences.zh: 所以听起来周末的故事确实是一个关于乌克兰突然取得成功，而且在很多方面令人惊讶的故事。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Although while we can see it as a story of success for the Ukrainians, what we learned over the weekend was the Russians are being plagued by some of the same fundamental problems
sentences.zh: 虽然我们可以将其视为乌克兰人的成功故事，但我们在周末了解到的是，俄罗斯人正受到一些同样根本性问题的困扰，

sentences.en: that have dogged them throughout the war, and they're not going to be fixed anytime soon.
sentences.zh: 这些问题在整个战争期间一直困扰着他们，而且短期内无法解决。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是Andrew Ross-Sorkin。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最有影响力的领导人，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: Vance、Elon Musk、Christine Lagarde、Zylran Mondani以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将于11月18日在NYTimes.com上直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，你可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你不会想错过的。

sentences.en: So, Eric, you said that we learned over the past few days that Russia's military is still beset by some of those same problems that it was earlier in the war.
sentences.zh: Eric，你说过我们过去几天了解到俄罗斯军队仍然受到战争初期那些同样问题的困扰。

sentences.en: What do you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: Break that down for me.
sentences.zh: 给我拆解一下。

sentences.en: Well, I think what we learned, again, just several examples of just kind of brittle the Russian military is in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为我们了解到的是，再次看到了俄罗斯军队在乌克兰是多么脆弱的几个例子。

sentences.en: I mentioned before that when this Ukrainian offensive punched through, Russian soldiers just dropped their arms and ran away.
sentences.zh: 我之前提到过，当乌克兰这次进攻突破时，俄罗斯士兵只是扔下武器逃跑了。

sentences.en: And what this underscores is just how poor the morale already was of those forces, how poor the command arrangements were there.
sentences.zh: 这凸显了这些部队的士气已经有多么低落，那里的指挥安排有多么糟糕。

sentences.en: They couldn't control their forces from running away.
sentences.zh: 他们无法控制自己的部队不溃逃。

sentences.en: And also that probably these guys weren't that well equipped.
sentences.zh: 而且这些人可能装备并不精良。

sentences.en: The logistics and supply problems that the Russians had so early on were continuing, even though they're closer to some of their supply lines in these eastern and southern places.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人从战争初期就存在的后勤和补给问题仍在持续，尽管在这些东部和南部地区，他们离部分补给线更近了一些。

sentences.en: So, we learned that a lot of these problems that surfaced initially in the Kiev operation haven't been resolved.
sentences.zh: 所以我们了解到，基辅行动中最初浮现的许多问题至今仍未解决。

sentences.en: Yeah, honestly, I mean, it feels like a little bit of deja vu for me, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，老实说，我觉得这对我来说有点似曾相识，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, you know, Ukrainians surge into a territory and Russians, you know, drop their weapons, run, leave their military equipment,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，乌克兰人冲进一片领土，而俄罗斯人，你知道，丢下武器，逃跑，抛弃军事装备，

sentences.en: dress in civilian clothes, get on bicycles, and get out of Dodge.
sentences.zh: 换上平民服装，骑上自行车，逃之夭夭。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And remember, here we are in Ukraine where the Russians have thrown about 80% of their available military, you know, into the fight right now.
sentences.zh: 记住，我们现在是在乌克兰，俄罗斯人已经把他们大约80%的可用兵力投入到了这场战斗中。

sentences.en: But they're still having to scrape to kind of put competent forces on these three different fronts.
sentences.zh: 但他们仍然不得不东拼西凑，试图在三个不同的战线上维持有战斗力的部队。

sentences.en: Even before this happened, they were pulling prisoners out of jail and putting them out on the front.
sentences.zh: 甚至在这件事发生之前，他们就已经在从监狱里拉人，把他们派往前线了。

sentences.en: They were reaching out and offering major bonuses to anybody who would serve, and they're turning to mercenaries as well.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在招募，向任何愿意服役的人提供高额奖金，而且他们也开始求助于雇佣兵。

sentences.en: So, it's this kind of motley crew that they're having to mix in with the remaining, you know, regular forces to try and hold the line here on these three major fronts.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一群乌合之众，他们不得不把这些人与剩下的正规军混编在一起，试图在这三个主要战线上守住防线。

sentences.en: And, of course, the Ukrainians do have full mobilization, right?
sentences.zh: 当然，乌克兰人实行了全面动员，对吧？

sentences.en: Their whole country is fighting.
sentences.zh: 他们的整个国家都在战斗。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Able-bodied men have not been able to, you know, allow to leave the country.
sentences.zh: 身体健全的男性一直无法被允许离开这个国家。

sentences.en: They basically are serving in the military or they're serving in some other capacity in the war effort.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上要么在军队服役，要么在战争中担任其他职务。

sentences.en: You've got everyday citizens who are, even if they're not in the military, they're supporting their country.
sentences.zh: 你看到的普通公民，即使他们不在军队中，也在支持他们的国家。

sentences.en: And so, for them, this is a huge rallying cry and a huge morale booster when they see their beleaguered military, you know, this is obviously a much smaller military,
sentences.zh: 因此，对他们来说，当看到他们饱受困扰的军队——显然这是一支规模小得多的军队，

sentences.en: not as well-armed going into this fight, suddenly being able to, for the second time now, pull off what's essentially an upset.
sentences.zh: 在投入这场战斗时装备也不如对手——第二次成功实现了一场本质上的以弱胜强，这是一种巨大的号召力和士气提振。

sentences.en: And, Eric, what are we hearing about what people are saying in Russia about this latest loss?
sentences.zh: 埃里克，我们听到俄罗斯国内对这次最新失利有什么说法吗？

sentences.en: Well, of course, Vladimir Putin, the president of Russia, has been talking about this as a special military operation from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当然，俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京从一开始就称其为“特别军事行动”。

sentences.en: The whole rationale that he's given here, that this is not, you know, a full-out war that threatens the Russian government and Russian regime and the Russian people.
sentences.zh: 他给出的全部理由是，这并不是一场威胁到俄罗斯政府、政权和人民的全面战争。

sentences.en: You know, go on living your lives is his message here.
sentences.zh: 他传达的信息是：你们照常生活就好。

sentences.en: We'll take care of business in Ukraine, even with the West supporting them.
sentences.zh: 即使有西方支持乌克兰，我们也能搞定。

sentences.en: He's basically been saying, this is a Russian military that's undefeatable.
sentences.zh: 他基本上一直在说，这是一支不可战胜的俄罗斯军队。

sentences.en: And this is, you know, even the official Russian outlets are now having to acknowledge this retreat.
sentences.zh: 而现在，即便是俄罗斯官方媒体也不得不承认这次撤退。

sentences.en: And while Putin has tried to kind of slough it off by continuing to carry on business as normal in Moscow,
sentences.zh: 虽然普京试图通过在莫斯科继续维持正常生活来淡化此事，

sentences.en: some of his critics, and these are people on the right, much more hawkish than he is, are outraged.
sentences.zh: 但他的一些批评者——这些人属于右翼，比他更强硬——对此感到愤怒。

sentences.en: And so to have this happen is enraged some of the critics in Russia who are now demanding that Putin take much greater steps to not just correct this problem,
sentences.zh: 因此，这件事的发生激怒了俄罗斯国内的一些批评者，他们现在要求普京采取更强有力的措施，不仅要纠正这个问题，

sentences.en: but to finish this war much faster.
sentences.zh: 还要更快地结束这场战争。

sentences.en: So really a new and quite tricky place to be for the Russian president.
sentences.zh: 所以对俄罗斯总统来说，这确实是一个新的且相当棘手的处境。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And politically, it's hard to know, you know, what Putin's political moves are going to be internally.
sentences.zh: 在政治上，很难知道普京内部的政治举动会是什么。

sentences.en: How does he regain momentum here?
sentences.zh: 他如何在这里重获势头？

sentences.en: What does the Russian military do next?
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯军队接下来会做什么？

sentences.en: The options are not good right now because Putin's bet, his bet here is that he can outlast, certainly Ukraine, and certainly outlast the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 目前的选择并不好，因为普京的赌注是，他能比乌克兰，当然也能比西方撑得更久。

sentences.en: And what he views is he can win a war of attrition.
sentences.zh: 他认为自己能赢得一场消耗战。

sentences.en: And that's not how this is working out, at least not right now.
sentences.zh: 但至少目前来看，事情并非如此发展。

sentences.en: So, Eric, given everything we've been talking about, let's step back for a minute and kind of put this weekend's news in perspective.
sentences.zh: 那么埃里克，鉴于我们一直在谈论的一切，让我们退后一步，从宏观角度审视一下这个周末的新闻。

sentences.en: How significant are these gains on the northern front for Ukraine?
sentences.zh: 乌克兰在北部战线取得的这些进展有多重要？

sentences.en: Are they actually a turning point?
sentences.zh: 它们真的是一个转折点吗？

sentences.en: Well, I don't think there's any question it is a major turning point strategically, certainly the biggest since the spring.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为毫无疑问，这是一个重大的战略转折点，肯定是自春天以来最大的一个。

sentences.en: It's a huge morale boost for the Ukrainians, and it could ripple to success on other fronts.
sentences.zh: 这对乌克兰人来说是一个巨大的士气提振，并可能产生连锁反应，带来其他战线的成功。

sentences.en: You could have this kind of cascading effect to other parts of Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 你可能会看到这种连锁效应波及到乌克兰的其他地区。

sentences.en: But at the end of the day, Russia still controls about 20% of Ukrainian territory.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，俄罗斯仍然控制着乌克兰约20%的领土。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There are two other fronts where the fighting is still intense, and it's a slog for the Ukrainians.
sentences.zh: 还有两个战线战斗依然激烈，对乌克兰人来说是一场苦战。

sentences.en: In Kherson, a portion in the south, Ukrainians have made some progress, but with heavy casualties.
sentences.zh: 在南部的赫尔松部分地区，乌克兰人取得了一些进展，但伤亡惨重。

sentences.en: And the Donbass, the Russians still are solidly in control.
sentences.zh: 而在顿巴斯，俄罗斯人依然牢牢控制着局面。

sentences.en: So, a lot depends on how Russia responds to this latest Ukrainian offensive in the northeaSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，很大程度上取决于俄罗斯如何应对乌克兰在东北部的这次最新攻势。

sentences.en: Do the Russians basically fall back and set up an effective new defensive line and hold off the Ukrainians now?
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人是会选择撤退，建立一条有效的防线，并挡住乌克兰人吗？

sentences.en: Or do they continue to collapse?
sentences.zh: 还是他们会继续崩溃？

sentences.en: Eric, do you think that we'll look back in a couple of months and see this point as the beginning of the end of the war?
sentences.zh: 埃里克，你认为几个月后我们回望时，会把这个时刻看作战争结束的开始吗？

sentences.en: I think it's really hard to tell right now, Sabrina.
sentences.zh: 我觉得现在真的很难说，萨布丽娜。

sentences.en: Clearly, the gains right now, they're not enough to win the war, not by any stretch of the imagination, given the other fronts that we've been talking about.
sentences.zh: 显然，目前的进展还不足以赢得战争，考虑到我们一直在谈论的其他战线，无论如何都谈不上。

sentences.en: And at the moment, they aren't enough either to kind of bring Vladimir Putin to the bargaining table.
sentences.zh: 而且目前，这些进展也不足以让弗拉基米尔·普京坐到谈判桌前。

sentences.en: Certainly, I don't even think Ukrainians think they should be going to the bargaining table.
sentences.zh: 当然，我甚至认为乌克兰人也不认为他们现在应该去谈判桌。

sentences.en: They feel there should be, you know, they need to seize more territory.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得他们应该，你知道，他们需要夺回更多的领土。

sentences.en: Again, this winter deadline is looming for the reasons we talked about before.
sentences.zh: 同样，由于我们之前讨论过的原因，冬季的最后期限即将来临。

sentences.en: Politically, for President Zelensky to lock in that Western support, he no doubt will use this opportunity to ask for more weapons, more advanced weapons from the West,
sentences.zh: 在政治上，泽连斯基总统为了锁定西方的支持，无疑会利用这个机会向西方索要更多的武器，更先进的武器，

sentences.en: and point to the success as saying, you know, why they deserve them.
sentences.zh: 并以这次成功为例，说明他们为什么值得这些支持。

sentences.en: But the military is going to also be under pressure to reclaim as much territory before these front lines are effectively frozen in place by the winter for some months to come.
sentences.zh: 但军方也将面临压力，需要在前线因冬季到来而冻结数月之前，尽可能多地收复领土。

sentences.en: So it sounds like the next few months will be pretty critical to the future of this war.
sentences.zh: 所以听起来接下来的几个月对这场战争的未来至关重要。

sentences.en: I think that's right, but it's still very hard to predict.
sentences.zh: 我认为是这样，但仍然很难预测。

sentences.en: I mean, a lot of people were surprised by this Ukrainian offensive over the last several days in the NortheaSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很多人对乌克兰过去几天在东北部的这次攻势感到惊讶。

sentences.en: But if you think about it, here's this scrappy Ukrainian military, you know, in a whole country, really, that's being supported by almost a billion dollars a week now in arMs.
sentences.zh: 但如果你仔细想想，这支坚韧的乌克兰军队，你知道，整个国家，实际上现在每周都在接受近十亿美元的武器支持。

sentences.en: And maybe it isn't that surprising they could pull something like this off.
sentences.zh: 也许他们能做到这一点并不那么令人惊讶。

sentences.en: And certainly, this is what the Ukrainians are hoping for.
sentences.zh: 当然，这正是乌克兰人所希望的。

sentences.en: They can show that with enough support, with enough financial support, with enough military support, they can pull this off and they can beat the Russians.
sentences.zh: 他们可以证明，只要有足够的支持，足够的财政支持，足够的军事支持，他们就能做到这一点，他们就能打败俄罗斯人。

sentences.en: That's what they're trying to show the world right now.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们现在试图向世界展示的东西。

sentences.en: In other words, Zelensky is hoping that this is going to be a proof of concept.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，泽连斯基希望这将成为一个概念验证。

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我认为是这样。

sentences.en: But the Ukrainians are trying to show this is a proof of concept of something they've been telling the West they can do for six months now.
sentences.zh: 但乌克兰人正试图证明，这是他们六个月来一直告诉西方他们能做到的事情的概念验证。

sentences.en: That if you give them enough arms, if they give them enough ammunition, if you give them enough support, they can take on the Russians and take them down.
sentences.zh: 那就是如果你给他们足够的武器，给他们足够的弹药，给他们足够的支持，他们就能对抗俄罗斯人并击败他们。

sentences.en: Eric, thank you.
sentences.zh: 埃里克，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: On Monday, Ukraine's military claimed to have taken an additional 20 towns and villages back from Russian control, adding to the territory it captured over the weekend.
sentences.zh: 周一，乌克兰军方声称又从俄罗斯手中夺回了20个城镇和村庄，增加了其周末夺取的领土。

sentences.en: Ukraine also claimed to have taken Russian prisoners.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰还声称俘虏了俄罗斯士兵。

sentences.en: A Ukrainian presidential advisor told the Associated Press that there were so many Russian prisoners of war that his country was running out of space to accommodate them.
sentences.zh: 一位乌克兰总统顾问告诉美联社，俄罗斯战俘太多，以至于他的国家已经没有空间来安置他们了。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了吗？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能免费试用《时报》一个月，而且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: Free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 30天免费访问。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还应该知道的事情。

sentences.en: The Times reports that the Justice Department has seized the phones of two top advisors to former President Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 《时报》报道称，司法部已经查封了前总统唐纳德·特朗普两名高级顾问的手机。

sentences.en: It has also sent about 40 subpoenas to Trump's close aides.
sentences.zh: 它还向特朗普的亲密助手发出了约40张传票。

sentences.en: These were the most aggressive steps the department has taken to date in its criminal investigation into Trump's effort to subvert the 2020 election.
sentences.zh: 这是司法部迄今为止在针对特朗普试图颠覆2020年选举的刑事调查中采取的最激进的步骤。

sentences.en: Federal agents took phones from Boris Epstein, a lawyer who helped coordinate Trump's legal efforts,
sentences.zh: 联邦特工从鲍里斯·爱普斯坦（Boris Epstein）那里拿走了手机，他是一位协助协调特朗普法律工作的律师，

sentences.en: and Mike Roman, a campaign strategist who directed Election Day operations for the Trump campaign.
sentences.zh: 以及迈克·罗曼（Mike Roman），一位为特朗普竞选团队指挥选举日行动的竞选策略师。

sentences.en: The subpoenas were issued to a wide variety of people in Trump's orbit, including Dan Scavino, Trump's former social media director,
sentences.zh: 传票发给了特朗普圈子里的各种各样的人，包括特朗普的前社交媒体总监丹·斯卡维诺（Dan Scavino），

sentences.en: and Bernard Carrick, the former New York City police commissioner.
sentences.zh: 以及前纽约市警察局局长伯纳德·凯里克（Bernard Carrick）。

sentences.en: The widening of the January 6th investigation comes as Trump clashes with the Justice Department over a separate legal matter,
sentences.zh: 1月6日调查范围的扩大正值特朗普与司法部在另一个法律问题上发生冲突之际，

sentences.en: the handling of presidential records, including classified materials that Trump kept in Mar-a-Lago, his Florida residence.
sentences.zh: 即对总统记录的处理，包括特朗普保存在其佛罗里达住所海湖庄园的机密材料。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Rob Zipko, Sidney Harper, and Muj Zady.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由罗布·齐普科（Rob Zipko）、西德尼·哈珀（Sidney Harper）和穆吉·扎迪（Muj Zady）制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by M.J.
sentences.zh: 由M.J.编辑。

sentences.en: Davis-Lynn with help from Lisa Chow.
sentences.zh: 戴维斯-林恩（Davis-Lynn）在丽莎·周（Lisa Chow）的帮助下完成。

sentences.en: It contains original music by Dan Powell, Rowan Nemisto, and Marion Lozano, and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 它包含丹·鲍威尔（Dan Powell）、罗文·内米斯托（Rowan Nemisto）和马里昂·洛萨诺（Marion Lozano）的原创音乐，并由克里斯·伍德（Chris Wood）进行工程处理。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brumberg and Ben Lansvork of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格（Jim Brumberg）和本·兰斯沃克（Ben Lansvork）创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西（Sabrina Tavernisi）。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受到严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当选举迎来了一群自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场伤痕累累、混乱不堪，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在《地铁》的最新一集中，我和莎拉·凯尼格（Sarah Koenig）一起，讲述了人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《地铁》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 在你获取播客的任何地方收听。
